text:
Pedini, I can't thank you enough for these lovely charts
 , If not for your charts I would have been struggling with the PAZ
concept. Les_Paul had hinted in one of his posts that PAZ concept is not
 restricted to just FTRs, but there are many other forms of PAZs like
Stacked demand/supply and compression, But i wasn't sure how to go about
 with locating these types of PAZ, but after going through your recent
charts , at least I'm starting to understand where to get started :) .

If you don't mind i do have a query regarding your latest kiwi trade,
please check the attached image below with your trade and one of IF's
trade enclosed within. If i'm right, i think you have considered the
compression scenario to mark this PAZ, so Is there any specific reason
why you chose to mark the lower end of the PAZ at point B and not at
Point A?

Please excuse if my reasoning is wrong . I'm also quoting one of Les_Paul's reply to a similar query earlier.

Thank you

Narayan

Les_Paul wrote:
rbnj0904 wrote: Hi Les_Paul,

I was going through one of your charts in Dr. swing's thread regarding
PAZ, Please check the chart attached below with my query, we would
usually consider the FTR point to define the limits of the PAZ, isn't
it? so the point 3 could have been marked as the upper limit of this
particular PAZ, but you chose point 2 in this case?. Am i missing
something here, or does a compressed approach changes things?

Thank you.

Narayan

Hi Narayan,

PAZ is compression.... so the upper limit should be touch of the last
wick of compresison. The FTR should not be included IMHO. Look at If's
printscreen here:
 www.readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/jo...3-if?start=250#19544
 he also did not included the FTR.

You know, he's the master, I am just an apprentice...

Les_Paul

author: Pedini
text:
Hey man.

I am so happy you are getting something out of my posts. It really does
mean a lot to me. As for why I chose point B, to me it was simply the
last point of supply that price needed to break to go higher. Point B
was a test of the supply in point A, and now has its own supply that
needs to be broken. I really didn't look into it more than that. It was
also reacted to at "3" which showed its significance.

I hope this is of some help!

Peds
